subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots continue inheriting all host pnpm overrides, or should OpenClaw scope/filter managed overrides so plugin-owned Express 4 dependency graphs keep their package-selected path-to-regexp line?
rationale: Both directions have product and security tradeoffs: host overrides protect OpenClaw's reviewed dependency boundary, but unscoped propagation can break third-party plugin dependency ownership and route startup.

options.title: Scope managed overrides
options.body: Filter or narrow host override propagation for managed plugin roots, preserving necessary OpenClaw security overrides without overriding incompatible plugin-owned transitive ranges; this best matches the plugin dependency ownership docs.

options.title: Validator-first only
options.body: Keep override propagation unchanged and add install/startup diagnostics that detect Express 4 plus incompatible path-to-regexp, accepting that plugin authors still need to repair their package metadata.

options.title: Keep plugin-owned workaround
options.body: Leave core unchanged and rely on affected plugin packages, such as camofox-browser, to migrate to Express 5 or publish their own shrinkwrap/override.

recommendation.title: Scope managed overrides
recommendation.body: Filter or narrow host override propagation for managed plugin roots, preserving necessary OpenClaw security overrides without overriding incompatible plugin-owned transitive ranges; this best matches the plugin dependency ownership docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the clearest current owner signal for the managed npm root install and override propagation path.
